Module 1: Enterprise Architectural Topology: Invoking Sovereign TGS Inside Microsoft Power Platform

1.1 The Sovereign Paradigm: Invoking TGS Inside Microsoft Power Platform

In modern Global 2000 enterprises, software engineering operates at the critical intersection of developer toolchains and low-code business operations. Mission-critical business processes, compliance approvals, financial transactions, and operational incident war-rooms reside within the **Microsoft Power Platform** (Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, and Power BI). However, low-code platforms traditionally lack deterministic mathematical verification, dialectical multi-agent consensus, and deep abstract syntax tree (AST) code analysis. **Tagisan (`tgs`) Subsystem 5** bridges this divide by enabling low-code makers and enterprise cloud architects to **call Tagisan directly from inside Microsoft Power Platform tools**. By calling TGS from within Power Platform: - **Low-Code Makers** in Canvas Apps trigger real-time Hegelian dialectical debates on code proposals via concise Power Fx formulas. - **Enterprise SREs** in Power Automate automate pull request audits, blast-radius mitigation, and incident escalations with sub-second TGS evaluations. - **Enterprise Architects** in Microsoft Dataverse enforce transaction-level gates using C# Plugins and Custom APIs that query TGS before database commit. - **AI Operators** in Microsoft Copilot Studio invoke TGS tools via Declarative AI Plugins, generating conversational responses strictly grounded in verified architectural decision records (ADRs). - **Compliance Auditors** on Power Pages sovereign portals verify Ed25519 asymmetric cryptographic receipts issued by TGS for every automated change.

1.2 In-Platform Calling Topologies & The 6 Invocation Modes

Subsystem 5 establishes six distinct in-platform invocation patterns, connecting low-code Microsoft cloud services to the sovereign Tagisan engine: 1. **Power Apps Canvas Studio (Power Fx)**: Makers write declarative formulas invoking `TGSConnector.ExecuteDebate(...)` or `TGSConnector.AnalyzeAST(...)`, populating in-memory collections (`ClearCollect(colTgsNodes, ...)`) and driving reactive galleries. 2. **Power Automate Cloud Flows**: Flow triggers (GitHub PRs, Dataverse events, Jira webhooks) invoke the TGS Custom Connector action or authenticated HTTP endpoints with HMAC validation, parsing TGS response JSON and branching on consensus scores. 3. **Microsoft Copilot Studio AI Plugins**: AI plugins bind TGS tools (`CallTGSEngine`, `AnalyzeCodeAST`, `ResolveArchitecturalDebate`) to Copilot's Generative Orchestrator, enabling conversational prompts grounded in verified TGS audit trails. 4. **Microsoft Dataverse Native Extensions**: Synchronous C# Plugins (`IPlugin`), Custom APIs, and Virtual Tables invoke TGS REST endpoints via `HttpClient` using Entra ID service principal tokens to gate transactions before database commit. 5. **Power Pages Compliance Portals**: External sovereign portals execute portal Web API JavaScript and Liquid templates calling TGS endpoints to verify cryptographic signatures and display live compliance attestations. 6. **Power BI & Microsoft Fabric OneLake**: Power Query M scripts call TGS REST endpoints (`Json.Document(Web.Contents(...))`), while Direct Lake semantic models read real-time Parquet Delta Lake tables with zero ETL delay.

2.2 Microsoft Entra ID App Registration for Calling TGS

To enable secure service-to-service communication between Power Platform and the TGS API Gateway, configure an Entra ID Application Registration: 1. Navigate to **Microsoft Entra admin center** (`https://entra.microsoft.com`). 2. Register a new application: `Tagisan-Enterprise-Gateway`. 3. Set **Application ID URI**: `api://tagisan-enterprise`. 4. Define and expose OAuth 2.0 Scopes: - `api://tagisan-enterprise/Consensus.Execute`: Permits Power Platform to initiate multi-agent debates. - `api://tagisan-enterprise/AST.Analyze`: Permits Power Platform to trigger Tree-sitter AST syntax and blast-radius analysis. - `api://tagisan-enterprise/Audit.Read`: Permits Power BI and Power Pages to read cryptographic audit records. 5. Under **Certificates & secrets**, generate a secure Client Secret or upload an enterprise X.509 Certificate for automated unattended execution. 6. Grant delegated permissions for `Microsoft Graph (User.Read)` and `Dynamics CRM (user_impersonation)`.

2.3 Hybrid Connectivity: On-Premises Data Gateway & Azure VNet Gateways

In sovereign enterprise topologies where the TGS engine runs within private corporate datacenters or isolated Azure Virtual Networks: - **On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)**: Install the OPDG cluster on a dedicated Linux/Windows host with outbound HTTPS (port 443) to the Power Platform cloud. The gateway proxies inbound Custom Connector requests directly to `http://localhost:8080` without opening public inbound firewall ports. - **Azure VNet Data Gateway**: For Azure-hosted containerized TGS clusters, deploy an Azure VNet Data Gateway in the delegated subnet to route Power Platform traffic over private IP backbones.

Module 3: Building & Certifying the TGS Custom Connector to Enable In-Platform Calls

3.1 Certified Custom Connectors: The Bridge for Calling TGS

Power Apps, Power Automate, and Copilot Studio interact with external REST services through **Custom Connectors**. A production-grade connector wraps the Tagisan REST Gateway using an OpenAPI 3.0 (Swagger) specification annotated with Microsoft vendor extensions (`x-ms-*`). Key Operations defined in `apiDefinition.swagger.json`: 1. `ExecuteDebate` (`POST /api/v1/consensus/debate`): Invokes the multi-agent dialectical debate engine to stress-test architectural proposals. 2. `AnalyzeAST` (`POST /api/v1/ast/analyze`): Parses source code syntax trees via Tree-sitter and returns impacted callgraph nodes and blast-radius scores. 3. `VerifyReceipt` (`POST /api/v1/compliance/verify`): Asynchronously validates Ed25519 signatures against the immutable sovereign ledger. 4. `GetTelemetry` (`GET /api/v1/cluster/telemetry`): Streams real-time daemon load, agent latency percentiles, and memory metrics. Microsoft Vendor Extensions applied: - `x-ms-summary`: User-friendly display names rendered in the low-code action picker. - `x-ms-visibility`: Setting parameters to `important` (prominently displayed) or `advanced`. - `x-ms-dynamic-values`: Dynamically populating dropdown choices directly from Dataverse records. - `x-ms-capabilities`: Declaring chunked transfer encoding and webhook notification callback URLs.

Populate reactive collections for thesis and antithesis arguments ClearCollect(colThesisPoints, varTgsResponse.thesis_points); ClearCollect(colAntithesisPoints, varTgsResponse.antithesis_points); // 3. Extract synthesis verdict, blast-radius score, and cryptographic proof Set(varSynthesisVerdict, varTgsResponse.synthesis.verdict); Set(varBlastRadius, varTgsResponse.synthesis.blast_radius_score); Set(varCryptoProof, varTgsResponse.synthesis.ed25519_signature); UpdateContext({ locIsAnalyzing: false }); // 4. Display conditional enterprise notification to the maker If( varSynthesisVerdict = "APPROVED", Notify("TGS Consensus APPROVED: Low blast radius (" & Text(varBlastRadius) & ") verified.", NotificationType.Success), Notify("TGS Consensus REJECTED: High blast radius (" & Text(varBlastRadius) & ") detected. Dialectical review required.", NotificationType.Error) ); ```

6.2 Step-by-Step Flow Logic for Calling TGS Inside Power Automate

1. **Trigger**: `When a HTTP request is received` (Receives PR diff from GitHub Actions). 2. **HMAC Verification**: Scoped JavaScript action validates `x-hub-signature-256`. 3. **Action — Call TGS Custom Connector**: Invokes `TGSConnector - AnalyzeAST` passing `{ code: triggerBody()?['diff'] }`. 4. **Action — Parse JSON**: Extracts `blast_radius_score`, `impacted_services`, and `cyclic_dependencies`. 5. **Switch Condition**: - If `blast_radius_score < 4.0`: Automatically invokes `TGSConnector - ExecuteDebate` and marks Dataverse row as `APPROVED`. - If `blast_radius_score >= 4.0`: Posts interactive **Teams Adaptive Card** to the SRE War Room with `Approve Override` and `Reject` buttons. 6. **Action — Persist Audit**: Inserts signed Ed25519 proof into Dataverse entity `tgs_auditrecord`.

Module 7: Calling TGS Inside Microsoft Dataverse (C# Plugins, Custom APIs & Virtual Tables)

7.1 Calling TGS from Microsoft Dataverse: C# Plugins, Custom APIs & Virtual Tables

Deep backend enterprise integration allows Microsoft Dataverse itself to invoke TGS synchronously or asynchronously: #

1. Synchronous C# Dataverse Plugin (`IPlugin`)

When an architectural record is created or updated in Dataverse, a synchronous C# plugin can call the TGS API Gateway to execute pre-validation before committing the transaction: ```csharp using System; using System.Net.Http; using System.Net.Http.Json; using Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk; namespace Tagisan.Dataverse.Plugins { public class TgsConsensusGatePlugin : IPlugin { public void Execute(IServiceProvider serviceProvider) { var context = (IPluginExecutionContext)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(IPluginExecutionContext)); if (context.MessageName != "Create" || !context.InputParameters.Contains("Target")) return; var target = (Entity)context.InputParameters["Target"]; string sourceCode = target.GetAttributeValue("tgs_sourcecode"); // Invoke Tagisan Sovereign Gateway via authenticated HTTP call using var client = new HttpClient(); client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add("Authorization", "Bearer " + GetEntraIdToken()); var response = client.PostAsJsonAsync("https://gateway.tagisan.enterprise.local/api/v1/ast/analyze", new { code = sourceCode }).Result; if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode) throw new InvalidPluginExecutionException("Tagisan Gateway unreachable; transaction rolled back."); var result = response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync().Result; if (result.BlastRadiusScore > 7.5) { // Abort Dataverse transaction if risk exceeds security threshold throw new InvalidPluginExecutionException($"[TGS Security Gate] Transaction blocked: Blast radius {result.BlastRadiusScore} exceeds allowed limit of 7.5."); } // Commit cryptographic proof to entity column target["tgs_blastradius"] = result.BlastRadiusScore; target["tgs_ed25519receipt"] = result.SignatureProof; } } } ``` #

2. Dataverse Custom APIs

Expose `tgs_TriggerConsensusDebate` directly as an unmanaged/managed Custom API in Dataverse, making it callable via OData v4 Web API (`POST /api/data/v9.2/tgs_TriggerConsensusDebate`). #

3. Dataverse Virtual Tables

Map TGS internal agent sessions, active debates, and audit ledgers directly in Dataverse without data replication, allowing Power Apps to query TGS data as native relational tables.

Module 10: Enterprise Security, ALM Pipelines & Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP)

10.1 Enterprise ALM Pipelines & Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP)

Calling TGS from inside Power Platform requires enterprise-grade security and automated lifecycle management: #

1. Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies

To ensure sensitive corporate source code sent to TGS never leaks to unauthorized external connectors: - Classify the `TagisanCoreConnector` into the **Business Data Group** alongside Microsoft Dataverse, Azure DevOps, and Office 365. - Isolate social and personal cloud connectors (Twitter, Google Drive, Personal Dropbox) in the **Blocked** or **Non-Business** groups. - If a maker attempts to create a flow passing TGS audit data to an unapproved connector, Power Platform DLP immediately blocks flow activation. #

2. Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) & On-Behalf-Of (OBO) Delegation

- In multi-tier Canvas App calls, the user's Entra ID identity is preserved using OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token exchange, ensuring user-level RBAC is respected inside TGS. - Real-time token revocation (CAE) terminates sessions within seconds if user risk changes or device compliance lapses. #

3. Power Platform Admin Center ALM Deployment Pipelines

- Manage automated multi-stage deployment environments (DEV $ o$ TEST $ o$ PROD) directly in the Power Platform Admin Center. - Automated PAC CLI solution export/import with pre-deployment automated regression test validation.
